etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English supplien, borrowed from Old French soupleer, souploier, from Latin suppleo (“to fill up, make full, complete, supply”). The Middle English spelling was modified to conform to Latin etymology.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To provide (something), to make (something) available for use.
(transitive) To fill up, or keep full.
(transitive) To compensate for, or make up a deficiency of.

quote.text: It was objected against him that he had never experienced love. Whereupon he arose, left the society, and made it a point not to return to it until he considered that he had supplied the defect.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To serve instead of; to take the place of.

quote.citation: 1666, Edmund Waller, Instructions to a Painter:
quote.text: Burning ships the banished sun supply.

quote.citation: 1700, [John] Dryden, “The Flower and the Leaf: Or, The Lady in the Arbour. A Vision.”, in Fables Ancient and Modern; […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: The sun was set, and Vesper, to supply  His absent beams, had lighted up the sky.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To fill temporarily; to serve as substitute for another in, as a vacant place or office; to occupy; to have possession of.
(chiefly in the plural) An amount of money provided, as by Parliament or Congress, to meet the annual national expenditures.
Somebody, such as a teacher or clergyman, who temporarily fills the place of another; a substitute.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From supple +‎ -ly.

definitions.definition: Supplely: in a supple manner, with suppleness.

quote.citation: 1906, Ford Madox Ford, The fifth queen: and how she came to court, page 68:
quote.text: His voice was playful and full; his back was bent supply.

quote.citation: 1938, David Leslie Murray, Commander of the mists:
quote.text: […]  the rain struck on her head as she bent supply to the movements of the pony, while it scrambled up the bank to the sheltering trees. For a couple of miles the path ran through woods alive with the varied voices of the rain,  […]
She swayed slightly in the gusts, bent supply to them and seemed at one with the force which Straup found so hostile.

quote.citation: 1988, Михаи́л Алекса́ндрович Шо́лохов (Mikhail Aleksandrovich Sholokhov), Quiet flows the Don (translated), volume 1, page 96:
quote.text: Grigory hesitantly took her in his arms to kiss her, but she held him off, bent supply backwards and shot a frightened glance at the windows.'They'll see!''Let them!''I'd be ashamed—'
